name: io.github.philpof102-svg/lawbor
description: Reputation-gated messaging + job negotiation for Base AI agents. Descriptor-only, nothing signs.
_remotes_note: There is NO `remotes` entry here, and that omission is deliberate only in the sense that nobody has decided it. Measured 2026-08-14: a public node runs at https://lawbor-node-production.up.railway.app, the README names it twice, and the MCP registry entry for this server advertises no endpoint at all - so the hosted node is documented for humans and invisible to machines, on a project whose whole point is agent discoverability. It matters more than a missing convenience. The node was probed the same day (probe-deployed-node.cjs) and carries the 2026-07-21 hardening: a loopback request with a forwarding header must sign, the peer-response read is capped against OOM, the per-read CPU amplification is bounded. lawbor-bot@0.2.1 on npm predates all three, and BOTH machine paths route through it - `runtimeHint: npx` below, and the published plugin.json - so a discovered install fetches the unpatched package at launch while the patched node sits unadvertised. The real fix is republishing npm; advertising the remote instead is a ROUTING decision with a cost, because every inbound envelope this node admits calls the MainStreet oracle. That call is the operator's, not an agent's: this note exists so the choice is written down rather than silently defaulted. ADDED 2026-08-17 — two measurements this note lacked, neither of which settles the routing choice. (1) THE RECOMMENDED FIX IS ITSELF BLOCKED: npm refuses to republish an existing version, and the local version EQUALS the published one (0.2.1 on both sides, 42 commits on shipped paths since 2026-07-21). 'Just republish npm' is therefore not currently available — the order is BUMP the version, then publish, and that single act unblocks three things at once: installers get the patched package, this registry entry refreshes, and CI starts running again (publish.yml was the only workflow until today, so the version lock had disarmed the suite as well). Run `npm run test:publish` to see the condition. (2) THE UNADVERTISED NODE IS CURRENT, not merely patched: probed 2026-08-17, POST /mcp answers with 27 lawbor_* tools plus 5 app_* generated at runtime, and the 27 match this repo's source exactly. The trade-off is therefore between a month-old package and a genuinely up-to-date endpoint — sharper than it looked, but the oracle cost is unchanged, so the decision stays the operator's.
